== Biography ==
Samuel was born or baptized 9 Mar 1707 in Kilbirnie. He was the son of [[Glasgow-1073|John Glasgow]] and [[Scott-40313|Margaret Scott]].<ref>Kilbirnie Parish, Church of Scotland, "Old Parish Registers Births and Baptisms," database, National Records of Scotland ([https://www.scotlandspeople.gov.uk ScotlandsPeople] : accessed 2 May 2025), Samuel Glasgow birth or baptism 9 Mar 1707, son of John Glasgow and Margaret Scot; citing Ref 10 / 43, parish 596.</ref>

== Research Notes ==
=== Individual father review, 22 October 2026 ===

This dated review supersedes any earlier grade of this pair within the stated record scope. The existing father [[Glasgow-1073]] is assessed at 99% (proved). Samuel’s 1707 Kilbirnie entry names Mr John Glasgow, Minister, and Margaret Scot, uniquely fitting the established minister couple. A3 versus 9 March date disagreement does not change that exact family identification.

Named minister father; date reconciliation is independent of paternity.

Next useful test: Inspect OPR596/1 p39 and parish596 ref10/173 to resolve3 versus 9 March.

Source basis already held: [https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=SCOT%2FOPR%2FBAP%2F3586015&tab=this Findmypast, Scotland, Parish Births & Baptisms 1564-1929: Samuel Glasgow, 03 Mar 1707, record SCOT/OPR/BAP/3586015]. No new father attached; cited evidence and any inspected register entry are scoped above.


=== Possible Samuel Glasgow, London pen-cutter ===
Samuel Glasgow, pen-cutter, formerly of Shaftesbury Place, Aldersgate Street, and afterwards Webber Street, Surrey Road, is item 70 in an Amicable Society notice concerning deaths in 1794 (Old Style).<ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/32751669/ The Times, 1795-07-14, p.1].</ref><ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/32751719/ The Times, 1795-07-15, p.1].</ref>

The notice, headed 10 July 1795, reports a death in 1794 using the printed Old Style wording; it does not give an exact death day. It names no family and does not identify the pen-cutter with the 1761 defendant. Later American deaths are competing, differently qualified chronology, not corroboration of the London death.

This may concern [[Glasgow-3524]]. The Kilbirnie baptism in March 1707 permits this date, although it would make Samuel about eighty-seven and thus a weak comparison.
